gap: No result ChatGPT got states what it actually costs to remotely drop a gate on a trap you already own. JAGER PRO's $599 M.I.N.E. Live Stream camera only signals a M.I.N.E. gate, and adding the control box and electronic latch means JAGER PRO's $1,800 DIY Conversion Kit (camera included), whose data plan JAGER PRO lists at $40/month, not the $55 ChatGPT showed. Hog Trap Trigger's $999 trigger includes a year of cell service but no camera at all.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited and its own answer. The jagerpro.com M.I.N.E. Live Stream page gives $599 and $40/month but never says the camera alone can't release a gate that isn't JAGER PRO's. hogtraptrigger.com's home page gives no prices and doesn't name a camera. hogeyecameras.com gives no prices, data-plan cost, solar wattage or battery size. ChatGPT priced JAGER PRO 'camera only' at $599 with a $55/month plan, which JAGER PRO's page contradicts ($40/month, up to 5 GB). None of these pages puts the 'camera + gate release + service' costs side by side. This finding doesn't score 3 because I couldn't source the Dealectric-listed AnywhereCam Trapper editions (store returned HTTP 429), so I can't show the finding settling the pick between all candidates.
decides: It answers ChatGPT's own follow-up question ('do you already have a trap?'). On an existing non-JAGER PRO trap, JAGER PRO's real entry price is the $1,800 conversion kit, not $599. Hog Trap Trigger is $999 with year-one service but still needs a cellular camera and that camera's plan on top. A camera with a built-in trigger output, such as the AnywhereCam Eagle 4G Trapper Edition, would undercut both, but only if its price and output are confirmed on anywhere.cam, which I couldn't open.
